chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who had intercourse with his wife, he said: When the two circumcised parts meet, the dower becomes obligatory and the waiting period [is established].

key_terms.الْخِتَانَانِ: The two circumcised parts (penis and vagina), indicating consummation
key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: The waiting period a woman must observe after divorce or death of husband
key_terms.الْمَهْرُ: The dower or bridal gift given to the wife

ai.seo_question: When does the full dower become obligatory in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the precise moment of consummation (tamaṣṣuḥ) by defining it as the meeting of the circumcised parts, a standard criterion in Shia fiqh for determining the obligation of the full dower (mahr al-mithl) and the commencement of the waiting period (iddah). It reflects the juristic consensus that physical penetration, rather than mere proximity, is the threshold for these financial and temporal obligations, ensuring clarity in marital contracts.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who slept with his woman. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When two circumcisions meet, it Obligates the dower and the waiting period’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a man who has married a woman and has gone to bed with her. He (the Imam) said, ‘When the two organs meet mahr (dower) become obligatory.’”
